值得閱讀的理由

  • 深入剖析《火影忍者》與《博人傳》主角評價兩極的核心心理與敘事差異。
  • 客觀拆解鳴人與博人父子間不同的成長背景、叛逆動機及觀眾的情感投射。
  • 探討王道少年漫畫中「底層逆襲」與「天才神童」設定對觀眾共鳴的深遠影響。

摘要

探討《博人傳》風評的真實現象

作者指出，儘管全球動漫迷對《火影忍者》懷有深厚情感，續作《博人傳》卻長期承受巨大爭議。作者澄清自己並非單純為了跟風抹黑，雖然承認《博人傳》水準確實不如前作，但當前網路上許多人僅是將其當作流行爛梗來嘲弄。作者希望跳脫盲從情緒，客觀剖析觀眾為何始終無法像喜愛鳴人那樣接納博人，究竟是劇情編排出了問題，還是博人的性格本身就不討喜。

出身背景與情感投射的巨大落差

作者分析，兩位主角在成長起點上有著極大反差。漩渦鳴人是極致的「草根逆襲」代表，童年孤苦無依、受盡全村冷落，這種底層奮鬥的經歷極易引發觀眾的同情與支持。相反地，漩渦博人身為火影之子，含著金湯匙出生且生活富足，容易被貼上「不知民間疾苦的富二代」標籤。當博人展現青春期叛逆時，一路伴隨鳴人成長的觀眾往往會以長輩立場斥責其不知感恩，導致兩者在觀眾緣上產生天壤之別。

行為動機與天才人設帶來的共鳴斷層

作者進一步對比兩人的塗鴉惡作劇：鳴人是為了被大家看見而擺脫孤立，博人則是源於父親長期缺席家庭、甚至以影分身參加妹妹生日所引發的情感失衡。雖然博人愛護妹妹的心態為他減輕了負面形象，但在天賦上，博人卻是個思維敏捷、一點就通的天才少年。不同於鳴人經歷無數挫折才習得忍術的刻苦過程，博人輕易掌握強大忍術的設定，反而削弱了傳統王道少年漫畫中最具渲染力的奮鬥共鳴。

Let me briefly explain for those who aren't familiar: "Boruto can't get hyped" is. probably the most common criticism you hear about this series, but why exactly can't it get hyped? The reason is that the production speeds for this series ' anime and manga are just too far apart. Normally, an anime should slowly adapt according to the original serialization , right? In the past, one episode of the Naruto anime would consume about one to three weeks of manga progress. However, the biggest problem with the Boruto manga is that it's a monthly release— only one chapter a month—yet the anime puts out four episodes a month. This meant that the Boruto anime was destined to have a massive amount of filler from the start. Those who have watched Naruto or Bleach know very well how insufferable the filler arcs can be. Well, now that about sixty percent of Boruto is filler, I have to note that these filler arcs are actually genuinely pretty good. There are also episodes like the Parent-Child Day that focus on family warmth, which are all great to watch. So, I must emphasize that the. Boruto anime's original content is definitely not trash through and through . It's just a fact that it's padded with a lot of filler. Boruto is a very peculiar product in anime history. Due to the strange way different versions dragged each other down, the IP's reputation was terrible from the start. For those who haven't watched it, here's a quick summary: Boruto had his entire life rewritten because Eida used her ability to alter the world's perception, making Kawaki. Naruto's son and Boruto the outsider. In an instant, Boruto lost everything he once had. And in an instant, the readers ' perception of Boruto did a complete 180-degree turn. Pain rushed to put his hand on Boruto's shoulder: "Now your pain far exceeds mine." The later stages of the Boruto manga are actually quite good. 摘要

探討《博人傳》風評的真實現象

作者指出，儘管全球動漫迷對《火影忍者》懷有深厚情感，續作《博人傳》卻長期承受巨大爭議。作者澄清自己並非單純為了跟風抹黑，雖然承認《博人傳》水準確實不如前作，但當前網路上許多人僅是將其當作流行爛梗來嘲弄。作者希望跳脫盲從情緒，客觀剖析觀眾為何始終無法像喜愛鳴人那樣接納博人，究竟是劇情編排出了問題，還是博人的性格本身就不討喜。

出身背景與情感投射的巨大落差

作者分析，兩位主角在成長起點上有著極大反差。漩渦鳴人是極致的「草根逆襲」代表，童年孤苦無依、受盡全村冷落，這種底層奮鬥的經歷極易引發觀眾的同情與支持。相反地，漩渦博人身為火影之子，含著金湯匙出生且生活富足，容易被貼上「不知民間疾苦的富二代」標籤。當博人展現青春期叛逆時，一路伴隨鳴人成長的觀眾往往會以長輩立場斥責其不知感恩，導致兩者在觀眾緣上產生天壤之別。

行為動機與天才人設帶來的共鳴斷層

作者進一步對比兩人的塗鴉惡作劇：鳴人是為了被大家看見而擺脫孤立，博人則是源於父親長期缺席家庭、甚至以影分身參加妹妹生日所引發的情感失衡。雖然博人愛護妹妹的心態為他減輕了負面形象，但在天賦上，博人卻是個思維敏捷、一點就通的天才少年。不同於鳴人經歷無數挫折才習得忍術的刻苦過程，博人輕易掌握強大忍術的設定，反而削弱了傳統王道少年漫畫中最具渲染力的奮鬥共鳴。

Many Naruto fans saw this and exclaimed, "Does this mean we finally don't have to watch Boruto anymore?" It’s like they’ve forgotten that the Boruto anime ended four years. ago, and would it even continue if the story wasn't good? Regardless, this makes me want to discuss an age-old question: Why can't Naruto fans like Boruto the same way they liked Naruto? Is it a problem with the plot, or is it that Boruto's personality itself is just unlikable? Today, I want to share some of my own thoughts on this. If you came here expecting me to trash Boruto, sorry, you’re going to be disappointed. Second, if you ask me whether I prefer "Naruto" or "Boruto," of course I think "Naruto" is better, okay? Right, please don’t misunderstand. . I admit that Boruto is mostly not very good; that’s an indisputable fact. But, and this is a big but, I feel that 80% of people these days aren't criticizing Boruto for legitimate reasons, they’re just hating on it to follow the trend, you know? They use Boruto as a convenient punchline. Whenever they want to compare something to garbage, they just throw out the name Boruto, and it always works. That’s what I mean. Alright, so are Naruto Uzumaki and Boruto Uzumaki—parenthetically, Bolt—a father and son? Duh, who doesn't know. that? The two share some very similar baselines, for instance, their appearance goes without saying—they are very much alike, he Naruto loves eating at Ichiraku Ramen, while Boruto loves grabbing burgers at Thunder Burger, and they even like the same size. Father and son have plenty in common, but apart from that, their upbringing and natural talent have created two protagonists: one who has been beloved from the start, and another who was criticized from day one. First, a common point people criticize Boruto. for is that he has it too easy. His mom is from a prominent clan in the village , and his dad is the greatest Hokage. He lives in a big house and enjoys a wealthy lifestyle; he’s essentially that classic "second-generation" rich kid who’s out of touch with reality, right? In contrast, look at how much his dad suffered when he was young. A kid living alone, eating instant noodles and drinking expired milk every day. Most importantly, because of the Nine-Tails, Naruto was ostracized, had no friends, and grew up all by himself. Looking at it this way, it’s clear which one.

resonates more with the audience. And I have to say, Naruto is, by nature, one of the most classic underdog stories in the world of shonen manga. Take stories like Cinderella, Harry Potter, or Cyberpunk: Edgerunners; they’re all the same. Watching the protagonist climb up from being a nobody to eventually reaching the summit—these "rags to riches" or "ugly duckling" stories are the easiest to connect with. Audiences immediately root for the protagonist. But Boruto has it tougher; he had his footing pulled out from under him right. from the start. After all, you can’t just destroy the protagonists’ happy ending right out of the gate, can you? That’s why Boruto had to start by creating a sense of suspense: the Hidden Leaf Village in ruins, a scar over his eye, and the claim that the age of the ninja is over. It throws the future at us right away to spark curiosity and keep us reading. Furthermore, Boruto has to be extra careful with his actions because he was born with a silver spoon in his mouth. Even slightly showing the immaturity or. impulsiveness typical of a teenager at his age can be risky. He might get scolded with things like, "You kids nowadays have no idea how hard your parents had it back then! You just know how to be rebellious all day, even throwing your dad's clothes out; you're just plain ungrateful!" Wow, why does that tone sound so familiar? Ha, there is one thing that I think clearly highlights the difference in how Naruto and Boruto are perceived due to their different backgrounds. Both Naruto and Boruto have climbed up to the Hokage faces to graffiti them. Nobody had any issue when Naruto did it, because at the. time, the audience didn't have any other perspective to consider. We all empathized with Naruto, thinking he was hated by the whole village and felt so sorry for him, so a little prank didn't seem to matter. However, it's a different story with Boruto. By the time of Boruto's generation, the audience had spent years following Naruto's perspective. So, in this new era, some people just adopt an adult's stance to criticize Boruto's behavior, saying, " Ugh, you brat, aren't you living a perfectly comfortable life?""And you still go and draw on your old man's face. , you're really ungrateful." The reasons for Naruto and Boruto's pranks are actually quite different. For one, it's a desire to be seen by everyone; even if most villagers dislike him, it's still better than being treated like air. For the other, it stems from an emotional imbalance due to a lack of fatherly attention. His dad is busy with work all day and refuses to come home, so this is the only way to get him to show up. To sum it up, I think Kishimoto and his team really tried hard to push Boruto into that "ungrateful brat" trap, and they succeeded in making him. sufficiently annoying. It's like, "Hey, Dad, it's fine if you don't care about me, whatever." He’s kind of given up on himself, but surely you should at least properly participate in your sister's childhood, right? What really makes Boruto angry is that Naruto even sent a Shadow Clone to Himawari's birthday. That was undeniably Naruto's fault, and no audience member can criticize Boruto for that. I mean, honestly, with Naruto’s outgoing personality, if it weren’t for the Nine-Tails holding him back, his social life wouldn't have been that bad , would it? Boruto never had that burden , so he immediately became the center of attention in class. Of course, that makes some people unhappy, complaining, "Boruto is such a Gary Stu. He doesn’t have to try at all, everything is just handed to him. This protagonist is totally unlikeable." Though, I have to ask: since when did a protagonist's. intelligence start determining how likeable they are? If you want to go there, didn't Joseph Joestar master Hamon on his own right from the start? And the ultimate move that killed Jonathan was easily countered by Joseph with just a glass! How come I never heard Jojo fans complaining, "Ugh, that's unfair, Joseph sucks"? Well, there are many reasons. First off, Part 2 is way more popular than Part 1, that's one thing. Plus, Joseph's personality is just so incredibly distinct. In comparison, Boruto doesn't have as strong of a personality, and I. agree with that; that is a fact. But speaking solely on talent, I still want to defend Boruto a little. First, even though he's Naruto's son, you can't forget that half his bloodline comes from the Hyuga clan. Do you really think a child of the Hyuga family would be that dull? Second, I actually don't think Naruto was ever that stupid. Looking back, the reason for his poor grades early on was likely because he lacked a fundamental element for growth. during his studies. What was it? It was peers. Everyone who’s been to school knows that when you have questions and no classmates to ask, it really affects your understanding of the material, right? I won't even talk about Shippuden ; just look at the Chunin Exams. Naruto defeated opponents many times through sheer flashes of brilliance. For example , against Neji, he used a feint to catch him off guard, and he even copied Sasuke's Lion Combo on the spot, adapting it into his own "Naruto Uzumaki Barrage." Naruto had those kinds of. instant-learn techniques too, but only Boruto gets put under this kind of microscope. You know, one of the few highlights of the combat in Boruto is seeing him rely purely on his intellect to combine standard techniques and find a way to win. Unlike Naruto; throughout his main series, his protagonist presence was always so strong that he never used the ordinary moves other characters did, relying only on Shadow Clones, Rasengan, Sage Mode, or Tailed Beast Chakra—those exclusive main-character moves. If you wanted to see Naruto use a normal Earth Style wall. , where would you even look? Exactly, you'd only see that in Boruto. Of course , later on, once Boruto unlocked "Karma ," those merits started to fade away; it’s true, you could argue this is one of the very few benefits of the Boruto anime's progress being so heavily stifled by the manga. Regardless, Boruto spent a long time overcoming the shortcoming of his main-character power-up not showing up until nearly 100 episodes in by relying on his wits and teamwork. The best example, I think, is the bell.

test with Kakashi; if you recall, Team 7 took that test and essentially passed by luck because Sasuke and Sakura didn't abandon Naruto, but Boruto grasped the true purpose of that test right away: it was meant to see if they understood teamwork. Because of that, the whole class centered their strategy around Boruto and came up with a brilliant tactic, coming within a hair's breadth of grabbing the bell, and the result, of course, was that everyone passed. I never disliked Boruto from the very. beginning. When he faced Kawaki in the manga and didn't hesitate for a second to hold a shuriken to his own neck, I quite liked him when he first appeared in the anime. Now that the manga has reached this point, I finally understand the level of resolve Boruto had when he said, "Even so, I'm still a ninja," in the first episode. Naruto endured the cold glares of his villagers growing up , while Boruto has endured the cold glares of netizens; the scale of this is simply incomparable. It’s an undeniable fact that second-generation characters are easily put under scrutiny, both in reality and fiction, but the reason. Boruto is so disliked, and its protagonist so resented, is that the creators give off the feeling of forcefully extending the story and milking an old IP. Okay, so listening up to this point, you should be able to tell that I've been defending Boruto the protagonist pretty hard. Because for me , the reason Boruto isn't good isn't that the protagonist is unlikable; it's that the stories happening around him are just hard to describe, and Boruto is just a victim of circumstance. What is Boruto most criticized for? Forcibly nerfing characters, an overly sci-fi. world, fighting aliens, power creep, time travel, and later on, things like battleships and light arrows. Well, this world already has clones, so I guess it’s not that strange for these things to appear. Coming up with all this random stuff isn't Boruto's fault; the aliens were something the original series brought in anyway. But speaking of this, people might play their trump card. What is it? Exactly, the biggest issue most people have with Boruto is that his character arc is hard to resonate with. Just comparing him to what his dad did in the past, there’s a huge problem— especially cheating on the exam, the difference is just too vast. When Boruto took the Chunin Exams, he actually cheated using scientific ninja tools, and ended up getting caught by his dad and scolded publicly, being told he was "not qualified to be a ninja." This one incident alone has made many Boruto-haters chase him for over a decade now; they still haven't let it go . Of course, you might ask, was Boruto cheating on the exam his fault? Yes, it 100%was, there’s no denying that. But. he’s just a teenager; is having a little opportunistic mindset really that serious? I mean, who hasn't felt anxious about their own lack of strength when they were young and wanted to take a shortcut? Plus, I think Boruto must have been afraid that if he didn't perform well enough or got eliminated, he'd be scrutinized and told, "Like father, like son; you're nothing compared to your great father." The important thing is learning and growing from mistakes, but Boruto isn't allowed to have any human flaws, or the typical recklessness that comes with.

that age. And the reason for that is simply because he is the son of Naruto Uzumaki . Wow, doesn't it feel like the fiction and reality just connected? See what I mean? Boruto does have a halo, sure, but his hardest struggle is that everyone only sees the brightness of that halo. I never thought about this. And at this point, you add in the issues with how the anime was adapted. Let me briefly explain for those who aren't familiar: "Boruto can't get hyped" is. probably the most common criticism you hear about this series, but why exactly can't it get hyped? The reason is that the production speeds for this series ' anime and manga are just too far apart. Normally, an anime should slowly adapt according to the original serialization , right? In the past, one episode of the Naruto anime would consume about one to three weeks of manga progress. However, the biggest problem with the Boruto manga is that it's a monthly release— only one chapter a month—yet the anime puts out four episodes a month. This meant that the Boruto anime was destined to have a massive amount of filler from the start. Those who have watched Naruto or Bleach know very well how insufferable the filler arcs can be. Well, now that about sixty percent of Boruto is filler, I have to note that these filler arcs are actually genuinely pretty good. There are many; for example , I can name one right now: the original opening of the Boruto anime, which I think blows both the movie and the manga out of the water. I really like that the studio chose to slowly depict their. daily lives at the Ninja Academy, and it's just cute, especially the bickering between Sarada and Boruto—isn't that adorable? The anime added original characters like Denki, Iwabe, and the Class Rep. They integrated so well that I can't imagine Boruto without them, and clearly, Ukyo Kodachi and Masashi Kishimoto agreed, which is why they imported the Class Rep back into the manga, right? There are also episodes like the Parent-Child Day that focus on family warmth, which are all great to watch. So, I must emphasize that the. Boruto anime's original content is definitely not trash through and through . It's just a fact that it's padded with a lot of filler. You have to watch about ten episodes just to find one that's truly good. Why can't Boruto get hyped? This, this is the reason. Just think about it: if you were trying to start a fire, but you were forced to take a five-minute break every two seconds, how could the fire ever catch on? You'd be nothing but a skeleton before the fire even starts, haha. Most of the anime's runtime is just waiting for the manga to reach a certain point—a stalling tactic. . Even if the writers wanted to write something serious, sorry, Boruto, Sarada , and Mitsuki can't get significantly stronger, and they can't achieve any major psychological growth, otherwise it wouldn't connect to the manga later on, would it? In the original Naruto, by episode 90, we were already watching the Konoha trio unleash their summoning jutsus in an epic battle. But in Boruto , by episode 90, the trio was still helping the elderly catch birds. Do you feel the problem here? To be honest, if Boruto had started airing a year later, perhaps it could have been.

like Demon Slayer, Jujutsu Kaisen, or Bleach: TYBW, with tight, well-paced seasons of 12 to 24 episodes. However, the fate of a long-running series with nearly 300 episodes is that the animation quality will inevitably fluctuate, and there will always be moments where it fails. If that happens during a major scene, like someone's death, it just turns into a meme. >> If Boruto's crying face is drawn even slightly off, people will laugh at it forever. Boruto is a very peculiar product in anime history. Due to the strange way different versions dragged each other down, the IP's reputation was terrible from the start. Ironically, the manga's reputation only finally took off after the anime ended. For those who haven't watched it, here's a quick summary: Boruto had his entire life rewritten because Eida used her ability to alter the world's perception, making Kawaki. Naruto's son and Boruto the outsider. In an instant, Boruto lost everything he once had. And in an instant, the readers ' perception of Boruto did a complete 180-degree turn. Pain rushed to put his hand on Boruto's shoulder: "Now your pain far exceeds mine." The later stages of the Boruto manga are actually quite good. At the very least, Boruto truly showed the resolve of a ninja, as well as a willpower not inferior to Naruto or Sasuke, which is worth acknowledging. To summarize: Naruto spent his whole life healing his childhood, while Boruto used. his childhood to heal his whole life. Naruto is the yang to the yin, Boruto is the yin to the yang, but in the end, they should arrive at the same destination. Netizens who say things like that are likely those who have been following the manga. Their resentment toward Boruto has probably long since faded, or they never actually hated it to begin with. Those who are still obsessed with hating Boruto until recently are probably just bitter old fans or pure haters. So perhaps it was always two different groups, and it’s not that they suddenly changed their minds. A while ago, wasn't the Naruto spin-off, Shadow Rising, announced? Then. suddenly, a bunch of people popped out of nowhere asking, "Is the original finally going to kick Boruto out of the canon?" Naruto ended in 2014, and Boruto was always just a dream. When I saw it, a giant "ha" popped into my head. This clearly looks like a story purely meant to fill in the gaps around the time they had kids. Besides, even if the main storyline of Naruto isn't 100%handled by Kishimoto, he still decides the general direction. As for what Boruto is actually about, his path to growth. definitely isn't as straightforward as Naruto's, that's for sure. But as it has developed, I would say this character has finally found a path that belongs uniquely to him. His dad's story is about a boy who had nothing and how he earned everyone's respect, so maybe Boruto's is the reverse: telling the tale of a privileged boy and how he must reclaim everything that belongs to him. As for whether it will turn out bad, well, that's another story entirely. Alright, what are everyone else's thoughts? Feel free to leave a comment and share. I'm.

異世界題材作品的流水線困境

作者在評點新番時，首先討論了《轉生為哥布林》等異世界作品。作者指出該作設定充斥既視感，從主角因救人車禍轉生，到繼承親友遺願化為外掛技能，發展幾乎與《關於我轉生變成史萊姆這檔事》雷同，因此決定將其列入棄番名單。此外，針對部分融入金融經濟冷知識或傳統退婚、神明召喚的異世界作品，作者認為其缺乏獨創性與張力，劇情流於公式化龍傲天套路，僅能給予偏低的評分。

在進入大作點評前，作者穿插分享了對《新楓之谷》懷舊內容的感動，回味起搭船前往天空之城、挑戰三轉試煉的往日情懷，隨後正式帶出備受期待的壓軸續作。

《電馭叛客：邊緣行者》第二季的群像魅力

相較於前作圍繞單一主角，作者認為《電馭叛客：邊緣行者 2》開創了全新的獨立篇章。故事聚焦於因神經狂暴化被逐出幫派的 King、全義體少女 Talia、背負滅門仇恨且招式酷似佐助的青年，以及熱愛攝影的 Roman 等四名新世代邊緣行者。作者盛讚本作戲份分配均衡，即使身處機械充斥的賽博龐克世界，故事核心依舊蘊含濃厚的人性溫度，並特別推崇兼具復古與酷帥魅力的全新女主角 Talia，果斷給予 S 級評價。

校園戀愛續作的風格轉變與降級

最後，作者探討了 Netflix 獨佔的校園戀愛作品《冰之壁》第二季。作者分析本作不同於作者前作純粹撒糖的風格，反而更偏向傳統少女漫畫的胃痛戀愛四角關係，充斥校園霸凌、誤會與拖沓的情節推進。儘管角色依然保有高情商的魅力，但劇情節奏在同地打轉過久，反而是直率爭取情感的情敵學妹更具吸引力，也因此作者最終將該作由原先的 S 級下調至 A 級。

with Gundam, a star-studded voice cast, and intense battle scenes—I really have to wonder, who exactly is the sugar daddy funding this? DKMachine. year for Keroro's rebirth, with a new movie and a brand new anime series. I have to say, projects that reboot childhood classics are almost always fighting a losing battle. No matter how good the animation of the new version is or how many technical improvements it has, in the eyes of old fans, it easily feels like something is missing, because what you're really up against isn't the anime itself, but those beautiful memories already coated in a thick layer of nostalgia. Successful cases like the new Urusei Yatsura or Wit Studio’s City Hunter are truly exceptions to the rule. The vast majority of old anime reboots end. up with a review that basically says, " It’s not bad, but I still prefer the original." Keroro is a bit unfortunate, as it has fallen into that same trap. Of course, I must emphasize that the new version isn't without its merits; for instance, the new voice acting is quite good, especially Tamama and Momoka, which are nearly spot-on, and the art style is okay, it’s just become a very modern, minimalist style. As for the. issues, honestly, the episode count is, to me, a huge red flag. And if the animation itself isn't particularly outstanding either, why wouldn't I just go back and watch the original? Right, the most ironic thing about this series.

is Mighty Media. They recently uploaded all 200+ episodes of the original to YouTube, so every time a new episode comes out, I can immediately go back and watch the corresponding original episode, only to realize, "Wait, is the original actually this much better?" So many wonderful plot points have vanished, and I truly miss the 2000s, with their very cheesy but adorable variety show vibe. There isn't even any fanservice anymore. It wasn't even that excessive to begin with, and you still. have to censor that? Then tell me, what exactly am I supposed to watch? 《學生會》的職人精神與異世界新作點評

AI 影片走進家門

作者注意到，YouTube 上充斥著以誇張標題講述動漫或網路小說情節的影片。這類內容從真人旁白、AI 配音，逐漸發展到直接由 AI 生成畫面與故事。原本對這些影片毫無興趣的作者，某次回到祖父母家時，發現奶奶除了看新聞，幾乎只看這類 AI 影片，於是決定用一個晚上親自體驗，弄清楚它們究竟有什麼魅力。

套路滿滿的 AI 動畫

作者點開一部名為《從金色天賦開始複製一切》的作品，先批評縮圖有種黏膩、混濁的「AI 垃圾感」。他觀察到，AI 動畫和漫畫常見套路包括穿越異世界、古裝背景、系統能力，以及主角從困境中翻身。這部作品也不例外：主角穿越後淪為死囚，隨即獲得能複製他人天賦的系統，展開復仇之路。

觀看過程中，作者發現影片只有 360p，畫面也有不少令人出戲的錯誤：半透明系統畫面上的文字沒有反轉，主角卻能直接讀取；角色使出攻擊時看似沒有揮刀，敵人卻倒下；士兵甚至全都長著一模一樣的臉。更令人疲憊的是，故事長達近三小時，劇情漏洞、人物行為與場景位置變化都讓人難以理解。作者形容自己彷彿逐漸被「黑泥」浸透，幾乎失去分辨劇情合理與否的能力。

劇情缺陷與短暫休息

第一部影片裡，主角最後成功闖關，還迎來傲嬌女主角的告白。然而，作者認為 AI 編寫的劇本充滿邏輯漏洞，角色位置也常在鏡頭切換間突然改變，彷彿會瞬間移動。認真思考會令人頭痛，不去思考又容易睡著。於是作者暫停觀看，去玩一款 RPG 遊戲，並順勢介紹遊戲玩法與抽獎活動，短暫逃離漫長的 AI 影片挑戰。

生成技術進步，題材也有看點

接著，作者觀看另一部講述女主角被迫成為直播主、故意說出毒舌真話想搞砸直播，結果意外爆紅的作品。雖然他仍未必認同作品本身，但注意到生成技術已有明顯進步，人物位置與場景邏輯不再像前一部那樣頻繁跳動。這部作品以職場人的處境為切入點，透過女主角想逃離工作、反而因此走紅的反套路設定，創造出新鮮感；作者甚至認為，這個點子拿去向電視台提案，或許也有機會受到青睞。

漫長挑戰仍未說完
